I can’t access the web or current FDA materials right now, so I cannot confirm what FDA guidance is the “latest” as of 2030‑10‑18. Based on historically available FDA guidance that has shaped device cybersecurity expectations, two foundational documents are: "Content of Premarket Submissions for Management of Cybersecurity in Medical Devices" (FDA, Oct 2014) and "Postmarket Management of Cybersecurity in Medical Devices" (FDA, Dec 2016). Those guidances established a risk‑based approach requiring manufacturers to incorporate security into design and development, produce evidence in premarket submissions (including threat modeling and security testing), maintain a software bill of materials (SBOM) and vulnerability‑management program, and operate postmarket processes for monitoring, patching, and coordinated vulnerability disclosure.

Because I can’t fetch or cite current webpages, I can’t provide a verified, up‑to‑date source list for the latest guidance; there may be newer or superseding FDA guidances, rulemakings, or guidance collections issued since those documents. To get the authoritative current guidance, check the FDA CDRH guidance page and the Federal Register (search terms: "FDA medical device cybersecurity guidance" or similar) and consult related authorities such as NIST and CISA for complementary cybersecurity standards and practices. If you want, I can—without web access—produce a concise checklist of the typical FDA expectations drawn from the historical guidances above.
